text:
anika_ops: Repro'd the customer OOM spikes on KV-heavy traces. Happens when concurrent decode windows + large KV entries pile up. Sharing quick traces and a few notes.

tom_lin: Thanks — which workload? long chat sessions or embed/rerank?

anika_ops: Long chat sessions with lots of system/prefix tokens (avg seq ~1500), and some very long context inserts from KV loader (single entries up to 1.2M bytes serialized).

michael_gpu: Seen similar. Profiling summary: kernel selection flips to fallback GEMM at sequence tails, and workspace allocs spike. Stack:
```
kernel_select: attention=fast_fused_v2 for seq<1024
seq>=1024 -> attention=fallback_attn
GEMM: aten_gemm_fast -> aten_gemm_fallback at peak memory
workspace_alloc: multiple small allocations (~32-128KB) per request -> fragmentation
```

jessica_prod: Hmm. So two problems: (1) fragmentation from many small buffers, (2) KV prefetch adds big pinned allocations that reduce room for decode workspace. Any quick mitigation ideas?

michael_gpu: Short list we tested: reduce per-request decode cap, add a slab allocator for small temporary buffers, and introduce a soft-reserve for workspace per model. Quick numbers from canary: before -> after (slab + cap=8k tokens + reserve=200MB)

```
metric | baseline | patch
p99 latency | 420ms | 430ms
gpu mem used mean | 11.8GB | 10.1GB
ooms/day (canary) | 5 | 0
throughput | -6% | -7% (throughput slightly lower but stable)
```

olivia_sre: The p99 latency going up slightly is expected. We want zero OOMs for enterprise customers. Does slab reuse add any GC costs?

michael_gpu: Slab reuse reduces number of unique cudaFree/cudaMalloc calls. We pre-allocate slabs for sizes: 4KB, 32KB, 256KB, 1MB. Reuse hit rate ~72% on our trace. GC overhead negligible; fragmentation dropped a lot.

anika_ops: Also found that KV *decode* vs *prefetch* sizing matters. If we pre-decode huge KV entries into the workspace we blow memory; instead doing streaming decode with a per-entry cap (and evicting after decode) helps.

jessica_prod: Can we keep some hot KV in a compact form (quantized, or compressed pointers) so prefetch doesn't allocate full decode buffers?

michael_gpu: Yes — maintain a compact serialized blob on device (compressed KV) and only materialize the full tensor for top-K hot entries. Also added an eviction watermark: when free memory < 350MB, start aggressive LRU on non-hot keys. That reduced fragmentation-induced OOMs.

perf-bot: nightly/regression-run: kv-heavy-regression increased OOMs by +8% last night on main commit ABC123. Tagging @eng-runtime.

tom_lin: For the rollback plan: 1) throttle decode tokens per-request to 8k, 2) enable slab allocator for temps, 3) enable eviction watermark at 350MB, 4) revert any recent kernel selector tweak that moved us to fallback GEMM for seq 1536. Rollout in canary tier first.

anika_ops: Agreed. I'll open a small rollout PR with feature flags for each toggle. We'll run load for 24h on canary and watch p95/p99 and OOM counts.

jessica_prod: Also add a healthcheck that returns a 503+Retry-After when workspace reserve cannot be satisfied so caller can retry instead of losing the whole request.

michael_gpu: Implemented a prototype: if workspace_reserve < requested_workspace -> return PARTIAL_RESPONSE with code 429 and reason "decode_cap_exceeded". Only enabled for tier=best-effort.

anika_ops: Capture of the canary runs is in /tmp/kv-canary-1862.tar.gz (internal). Key logs: sample OOM stack, slab hit rates, kernel selection traces. I'll paste the most relevant snippet: 
```
[2026-04-12T03:12:11Z] model=redwood-base: allocate workspace 320MB -> OK (reserve 200MB)
[2026-04-12T03:12:11Z] kv_worker: materialize key id=98765 size=1.1MB -> stored in compressed-kv pool
[2026-04-12T03:12:12Z] decode: requested_tokens=12000 -> throttle to 8192
[2026-04-12T03:12:13Z] kernel_select: using fused_attention_v2
[2026-04-12T03:12:14Z] oom: attempted_alloc=80MB, free=12MB -> triggered eviction (evicted 14 keys)
```

olivia_sre: Nice. Can you also add telemetry for "fraction of requests that hit slab vs direct alloc" and a gauge for "compact-kv-bytes_on_device"? We'll need to alert if compact-kv grows > 80% of reserved pool.

michael_gpu: Will add metrics: slab_hit_rate, compact_kv_bytes, kv_eviction_count. Also a histogram for per-request decode_tokens_used.

jessica_prod: Once metrics are in, let's run for 48h on canary and then promote. Also add a short doc blurb for customers about decode caps and best-effort behavior.

anika_ops: TL;DR: mitigation = slab allocator + per-request decode cap + compact-on-device KV + eviction watermark + partial-response fallback. Early canary results look promising (zero OOMs, small perf tradeoff).

tom_lin: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll track the rollout checklist in the PR and schedule a postmortem if OOMs reappear. :thumbsup:
